confidence_notes: I ran three web searches: one for the RBA rate and two for Byron Bay prices. The price sources were crowdsourced cost-of-living aggregators (nomad.watch, citycost.org, jobicy, expatexchange) and they disagree. Restaurant meal and coffee anchors are the best supported. These were roughly A$18-25 for an inexpensive meal, A$73-112 for a mid-range dinner for two, and A$4.5-5.5 for a cappuccino, with Byron Bay at a tourist-town premium. Beer is about A$8-12 for a pint, so I used a pub-pint figure. I found no regular menu prices for cocktails or wine. A search turned up only happy-hour listings, such as about A$14-16 cocktails and A$8 house wine. Cocktail and wine anchors are therefore based on the local relationship to beer and on typical Australian tourist-town pricing. They are estimates, not sourced menu prices. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Byron Bay's high, seasonal tourist pricing. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any live listings. They are the least certain anchors, and prices swing widely with season and events.
comparable_city_reasoning: Priced as a premium Australian coastal tourist town, above Brisbane and similar to or somewhat below Sydney for food and drink, and well above typical regional NSW for accommodation.
